newsitem.title: USA: Clinton welcomes North Korea's release of Hunziker.
newsitem.headline: Clinton welcomes North Korea's release of Hunziker.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Wednesday welcomed North Korea's release of Carl Hunziker, a 26-year-old U.S. citizen detained by Pyongyang for three months as a spy.

"The president warmly welcomes the release of Evan Carl Hunziker, who has been held by North Korea since late August and arrived today back in the United States," the White House said in a brief statement.
"We have repeatedly urged the government of North Korea to release Mr. Hunziker and are pleased he will be home and reunited with his family in time for Thanksgiving," it added.
Hunziker's release was negotiated by Representative Bill Richardson, a New Mexico Democrat and Clinton confidant whom the White House strongly praised.
"Congressman Richardson's efforts were indispensable and we are grateful for his tireless efforts under difficult circumstances," it said.

Hunziker, who his family says is a missionary, was detained by North Korea near the border with China on Aug. 24 when he crossed the Yalu River, separating the two countries. The Parkland, Washington, man was then held by North Korea on charges of espionage and illegal entry.
The United States, South Korea and Hunziker's family have all denied he is a spy. His family said he probably crossed the border to try to convert North Koreans to Christianity.
Hunziker, who was released on Tuesday, arrived at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on an American Airlines flight from Tokyo.
In a brief meeting with reporters, he said he was treated fairly by the North Koreans and was looking forward to spending the Thanksgiving Day holiday with his family.
He said being back in the United States "feels great."
